description: Catalogue of recurring resistance behaviours in organisational change, with early indicators and the ADKAR element most often missing. Use when populating the change-readiness assessment and the adoption section of the risk register.

items.name: Passive compliance
items.description: People agree in meetings and continue old practice afterwards; no open objection, no adoption.
indicators: Attendance high, usage of new process low
'We tried this before' in corridor conversations
items.response: Missing Desire. Surface WIIFM per group; involve informal leaders in design; publish adoption metrics per team.

items.name: Loss of status or expertise
items.description: Experts whose knowledge is embedded in the current process see the change as devaluing them.
items.response: Missing Desire/Ability. Give experts a designer or coach role in the target model; recognise legacy contribution explicitly.

items.name: Change fatigue
items.description: Cumulative exhaustion from repeated initiatives, regardless of the merit of the current one.
indicators: Cynical humour about 'the next big thing'
Requests to 'just tell us what to do'
items.response: Missing Awareness (why this one is different). Sequence the roadmap, retire zombie initiatives, over-deliver on the first quick win.

items.name: Structural disincentive
items.description: Targets, bonuses or reporting lines reward the old behaviour.
indicators: Managers penalised for short-term dips during transition
items.response: Missing Reinforcement. Align performance management before, not after, the change; make it a roadmap dependency.

items.name: Sponsor drift
items.description: Executive sponsor's attention moves on before the change is anchored.
indicators: Decisions deferred for more than two cycles
items.response: Missing Reinforcement at the top. Fix sponsor commitments in the governance cadence; escalate drift as a HIGH risk with a named owner.

sources: Kotter, J.P., Schlesinger, L.A. — 'Choosing Strategies for Change', HBR (1979, 2008 ed.)
